strengths: Displays a balanced, wide athletic base and good knee flexion when fully engaged at the non-volley zone line (notably during Rally 6 at 01:21-01:23).
Active lateral movement and quick recovery when scrambling to cover open court space.

top_priority_fix.issue: Dropping the paddle below waist height in the ready position at the kitchen line.
top_priority_fix.why_it_matters: Letting the paddle dangle down by the thigh significantly increases the time required to react to opponent speed-ups, forcing defensive flicking motions rather than compact, controlled punch volleys.
top_priority_fix.evidence: In Rally 2 between 00:09 and 00:11, as well as during Rally 6 reset moments (01:24) and Rally 7 setup (01:30-01:31), the right arm drops completely straight with the paddle pointing toward the court surface while facing opponents.

secondary_observations.issue: Taking an oversized backswing on transition balls and volleys.
secondary_observations.evidence: At 00:36-00:37 and 01:19-01:20, the hitting arm pulls far behind the torso plane prior to forward swing, creating a late contact point behind the body.

secondary_observations.issue: Static positioning without shifting to protect the middle seam.
secondary_observations.evidence: In Rally 1 (00:06-00:08) and Rally 2 (00:10-00:12), when the partner is pulled wide left, player remains anchored near the right sideline instead of sliding toward the centerline to pinch the middle.

drill_recommendation.name: Rapid Fire Wall/Partner Volley Reset
drill_recommendation.target: Instant paddle recovery to chest height pointing at 10-to-2 o'clock between every strike.
drill_recommendation.reps_duration: 4 rounds of 90 seconds of rapid un-bounced kitchen volleys focusing exclusively on paddle-up posture.
